h1: The 7 Best Cordless Vacuums for Hardwood Floors of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 cordless stick vacuums for hardwood homes, sorted by runtime, power and price tier, with picks for every budget.
summary: The Levoit Cordless Vacuum is the best cordless vacuum for hardwood floors, with a listed 60 minute runtime in a smaller footprint, in the $200 to $500 bracket. The Shark PowerPro Flex Reveal Plus offers 50 minutes from a familiar brand, and the mohomo lists the longest runtime at 70 minutes and 650W. The second Levoit, TechRise, iXlion and Shark Pet stick follow.
intro: The classic hardwood mistake is buying a cordless vacuum on wattage alone. Wood needs a head that lifts dust without flinging it across the boards, and a battery that finishes the floor plan before it quits. Watts describe how much power the motor draws, not how well it cleans, and a big figure with a stiff brush or a thirty-minute battery is a poor trade.

We weighed seven cordless vacuums on the Primea framework, with listed runtime, stated wattage, brand support and price bucket carrying the most weight. Brush type and bin size are missing from most listings, so we flag them rather than guess. Prices are buckets, and every claim below is the maker's, not a measurement of ours.

products.name: Levoit Cordless Vacuum
products.verdict: A 60 minute runtime in a smaller footprint makes it the most practical whole-home pick.
products.description:
The Levoit Cordless Vacuum lists a 60 minute runtime, which is enough to cover a full hardwood floor plan without a mid-job recharge. It sits in the $200 to $500 bracket, the priciest tier in this ranking. Runtime matters on hardwood because a stop-start clean leaves dust lines on boards.

It earns the top spot because it combines the long runtime with a smaller footprint and strong brand support. Against the mohomo, it gives up ten minutes of listed runtime but is a more established name.

Buy it for small homes that want one-pass cleaning. The caveats are the highest price tier here and that the brush type is not listed. Skip it if you want to stay under $200.
products.idealFor: Small homes that want one-pass cleaning.

products.name: Shark PowerPro Flex Reveal Plus Cordless Vacuum
products.verdict: A 50 minute runtime from a familiar vacuum brand at a mid price.
products.description:
The Shark PowerPro Flex Reveal Plus lists 50 minutes of runtime and falls in the $100 to $200 bracket. That combination makes it the easiest recommendation for buyers who want a known name. A familiar brand usually means that batteries, filters and rollers are easy to find years later.

It ranks below the Levoit because it has ten fewer minutes and no wattage listed. It beats the iXlion and TechRise on brand backing, which matters when parts wear.

Buy it for a familiar brand at a mid price. The caveats are no stated wattage and shorter runtime than the Levoit. Skip it if you need over an hour of runtime.
products.idealFor: Buyers who prefer a familiar brand.
products.skipIf: You need over an hour of runtime.

products.name: mohomo Cordless Vacuum Cleaner
products.verdict: The 70 minute battery is the longest of the group.
products.description:
The mohomo lists 70 minutes of runtime and 650W, the highest figures on both counts in this ranking, at a $100 to $200 price. Seventy minutes is long enough to cover a larger home in one go, and the wattage claim suggests a strong motor.

It sits third because the brand is less established than Levoit or Shark, even though its numbers are the best. Maker claims go unverified, and a higher wattage drains a battery faster, which can shorten the real minutes.

Buy it for large homes with lots of floor. The caveats are a lesser-known brand and unverified claims. Skip it if brand reputation matters most.
products.idealFor: Large homes with lots of floor.
products.skipIf: Brand reputation matters most to you.

products.name: Levoit Cordless Vacuum Cleaner
products.verdict: A 50 minute runtime from Levoit without the top price tier.
products.description:
This Levoit lists 50 minutes of runtime and sits in the $100 to $200 bracket, cheaper than the other Levoit in this guide. It keeps the brand and the cordless design at a lower tier, which suits apartments, where a floor plan rarely needs more than fifty minutes. A smaller home makes the extra ten minutes of the other Levoit unnecessary.

It ranks fourth because it matches the Shark on runtime but offers fewer listed extras. Against the Levoit leader, it trades ten minutes for a lower price.

Buy it for apartment dwellers watching cost. The caveats are few listed extras and no wattage. Skip it if you want the longest runtime.

products.name: TechRise Cordless Vacuum Cleaner
products.verdict: The cheapest entry here, with 60 minutes and 550W listed.
products.description:
The TechRise is in the $50 to $100 tier, the lowest in this ranking, yet lists 60 minutes of runtime and 550W. Low prices usually come with weak batteries, but this listing matches the top Levoit on minutes.

It ranks fifth because the brand is unproven, though the numbers rival pricier picks. Against the iXlion, it adds five minutes and a wattage figure at the same tier. A 550W rating suggests a modest motor, which is gentle on a battery and suits light hardwood dust.

Buy it for budget buyers who want runtime. The caveats are an unproven brand and unknown build quality. Skip it if you want a brand with a long support history.
products.skipIf: You want a brand with long support history.

products.name: iXlion Cordless Vacuum Cleaner for Home
products.verdict: A 55 minute runtime in the $50-100 tier.
products.description:
The iXlion lists 55 minutes of runtime in the $50 to $100 price tier. It is a plain stick vacuum at a low price, and the spec sheet is thin.

It ranks sixth because the TechRise offers more runtime and a wattage figure at the same tier. It is a reasonable alternative if the TechRise is unavailable, but there is little else to recommend it. With no wattage and little detail, you cannot judge power at all, so treat it as a fallback and not a first choice.

Buy it for small homes on a budget. The caveats are the thin spec sheet and no wattage listed. Skip it if you want a detailed spec sheet.
products.skipIf: You want a detailed spec sheet.

products.name: Shark Pet Cordless Stick Vacuum
products.verdict: A Shark stick with 40 minutes, best for small spaces.
products.description:
The Shark Pet Cordless Stick Vacuum lists 40 minutes of runtime in the $100 to $200 tier. Forty minutes covers a small space, but a full hardwood floor plan may need a recharge.

It lands last because its runtime is the shortest here and it costs more than the budget picks. The Shark name is its main appeal, along with the stick format. The pet focus suggests a brush built for hair, which may not be gentle on finished boards, so check the head before buying.

Choose it for small spaces and quick cleanups. The caveats are the shortest runtime here and a price above the budget options. Skip it if you clean a whole house in one go.
products.skipIf: You clean a whole house in one go.

whatMatters.detail: Runtime is how many minutes the battery lasts on its normal setting. On a hardwood floor plan of several rooms, 50 minutes or more avoids a mid-clean recharge. Look for the minutes figure in the title or bullets, and treat it as a best case, since boost settings drain the battery faster than the headline minutes suggest.

The head is what touches the floor. A soft roller picks up fine dust without scattering it, while a stiff bristle brush can scuff or flick debris on hard surfaces. The listing should name the head, so look for soft or hard floor wording, and avoid a stiff brush on finished wood. Soft rollers also pick up pet hair without wrapping.

Wattage is a rough indicator of motor draw, not a measure of cleaning. Higher numbers like 650W suggest more suction but also drain the battery faster. Compare wattage only between similar models, and read it alongside runtime, because a strong motor with a short battery is a poor trade.

A small bin forces frequent stops, which cuts into the battery you paid for. Check the bin capacity and whether it empties without touching dust. This detail is missing on many listings, so check the product page, and favor a model that empties in one motion. Dust that blows back into your face is a fair test of a bin.

Batteries age, and filters and brush rolls wear out. A known brand usually means replacement parts are easy to find years later. Search the listing for replacement battery and filter availability before buying, because a vacuum with dead batteries and no parts is just a stick. A known brand usually sells spares.

faq.q: Are cordless vacuums safe for hardwood floors?
faq.a: Generally yes if the head has soft bristles or a soft roller. Hard bristles can scuff finished wood and flick debris. Check the listing for a hard floor mode or soft head before buying.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake buyers make?
faq.a: Buying on wattage alone. A big number does little if the head scatters debris or the battery dies after 20 minutes. Read runtime and head type before you read watts, since those two decide the result.

faq.q: Is the Levoit worth more than the Shark?
faq.a: It adds ten minutes of listed runtime and a smaller footprint, but costs more. If 50 minutes is enough, the Shark saves money and offers a familiar brand with easy parts.

faq.q: How do I set up a cordless vacuum?
faq.a: Charge the battery fully before first use, assemble the wand and head, and mount the dock on a wall near an outlet if included. Keep the dock away from damp areas.

Empty the bin after each use, clean or replace the filter on the schedule in the manual, and clear hair from the roller. Replace the filter when it stops fitting snugly, and wash washable parts only when the manual allows.

faq.q: Can a cordless vacuum replace a plug-in model?
faq.a: For most hardwood homes, yes, if the runtime covers your floor plan. Very large homes may still benefit from a second battery or a corded unit, and heavy rugs favor a stronger plug-in vacuum.

finalTake: Buy the Levoit for a whole-home hardwood clean, or the Shark PowerPro if a known name matters. The mohomo has the biggest numbers but the least proven brand, and the TechRise is the budget runtime pick. Treat watts as a rough guide only, and check the brush head and bin size on the listing before you order.
